ShelfLife.kickoff:
Build ShelfLife, a small local pantry tracker for one household. Python 3.12 standard library only (sqlite3, http.server, csv, json); no third-party packages, no network access at runtime, no build step.

Backend: `python server.py --port PORT --db PATH` serves a JSON API and the web UI on 127.0.0.1.
- Items have: id, name (1-80 chars), quantity (integer >= 0), unit (text, optional), expires (YYYY-MM-DD or null), created_at.
- GET /api/items (optional ?expiring_within=DAYS, ?q=TEXT name search) returns items sorted by expiry (nulls last).
- POST /api/items creates; PATCH /api/items/{id} updates quantity/name/unit/expires; POST /api/items/{id}/consume {"amount": n} reduces quantity (never below 0; 409 if amount exceeds quantity); DELETE /api/items/{id}.
- Invalid input returns 400 with {"error": "..."}; unknown id 404. Data persists in the SQLite file across restarts. Concurrent requests must not corrupt data or lose updates (two simultaneous consumes of the last unit: exactly one succeeds).

UI (served at /): one responsive page that works at phone and desktop sizes.
- "Expiring soon" section (next 7 days, expired items clearly marked), full list with search and an expiry filter, add-item form with inline validation messages, consume and delete actions, empty state and a visible error state when the API fails.
- Keyboard accessible with visible focus; readable contrast; no horizontal scrolling at 375px. Clean, calm visual design.

Import: `python import_items.py FILE.csv --db PATH` loads rows (name,quantity,unit,expires) into the same database, skipping invalid rows and printing one summary line "imported N, skipped M" (exit 0), or exit 2 with an error on an unreadable file.

Done means: the server, UI and importer work together from a fresh folder; a short README explains how to run them.

Quiet Bench.kickoff:
Build Quiet Bench, a noise-cancelling test bench that runs on this PC with no audio hardware. Python 3.12 standard library plus Node 20
for the page checks; no third-party runtime packages, no network. I can generate a noise signal (tones, band noise) or import a WAV
file; the bench simulates the acoustic path from the noise source to the ear, runs an adaptive canceller (LMS family) against it and
tells me how much was cancelled in each frequency band. Every session is saved on a small local storage server
(`python server.py --port PORT --data DIR`) with its settings and results, and a web page on that server lets me start a run, browse
saved sessions, reload one and compare two. A command line (`python bench.py run|list|show|export`) does the same without the page.
A limiter must hold the output inside a safe level when the filter diverges, and a stop switch ends a run at once.

Audience and preferences:

constraints.value: POST /api/runs with settings -> session (asynchronous allowed); GET /api/sessions -> array; GET /api/sessions/ID -> session; POST /api/runs/ID/stop; GET /api/compare?a=ID&b=ID -> array of bands with low, high, delta_db = b minus a.

constraints.meaning: The web interface preserves the required accessible controls and observable selectors.
constraints.value: Accessible labelled textarea[name=settings] (JSON), Start run button, [data-session-id=ID] saved session buttons, select[name=compare-a], select[name=compare-b], Compare button and [data-comparison] result. Show session id and band numbers.

constraints.meaning: Sessions are stored locally and served through the specified entry point.
constraints.value: python server.py --port PORT --data DIR

constraints.meaning: The user can operate both interfaces without guessing commands.
constraints.value: docs/try-it.md gives actual start/stop and CLI commands.

quality.criterion: Results are numerically trustworthy and distinguish simulated attenuation from a real-world hardware measurement.
quality.verification: Run known signals and paths with independently checkable expected behavior; inspect band values and sample arrays, including a WAV run, and confirm the page and CLI report the saved result consistently.

quality.criterion: Output remains within the configured limiter and a stop request ends processing promptly, including during divergence.
quality.verification: Drive the filter into divergence and verify every output sample respects the limit and limited is true; stop an active run and verify stopped status and no further processing.

quality.criterion: The page feels like a calm, exact instrument: deliberate offline-available typography, a restrained high-contrast palette, generous spacing and clear controls rather than decorative cards or gradients.
sources: Design guidance used by UI workers
quality.verification: Inspect the actual desktop page, keyboard operation, accessible labels and reduced-motion behavior; verify the browser console is clean and requested files, including the icon, are served.

quality.criterion: A saved experiment can be found, reloaded and compared consistently through its supported interfaces.
quality.verification: Start a run, restart the server, reload it through the page and CLI, export it, and compare two saved sessions with delta_db calculated as b minus a.

scopeOut.outcome: Audio hardware playback, hardware control and claims of measured real-world cancellation.
Accounts, network services, deployment, paid assets and third-party runtime packages.

vision.sizeWhy: Micro: the closest supplied comparable is a standard-library signal-processing bench with a page, CLI and local storage server; one capable plain agent is estimated to build and verify it in minutes within one session. Hardware integration, external dependencies or a broader validated acoustic model would make it bigger. The observed Node version is v25.8.0, so verification specifically under the requested Node 20 remains unproven with the stated runtime access.

stories.outcome: The engineer can generate tones or band noise or import a WAV, simulate the acoustic path and adaptive LMS-family cancellation, and judge attenuation by frequency band before buying hardware.
stories.story: As an audio engineer, I want to try a noise and canceller configuration and see credible per-band results so I can decide which ideas merit hardware experiments.

stories.outcome: Anti-noise output is bounded at the configured safe level, limiting is recorded, and an active run can be stopped immediately.
stories.story: As an audio engineer, I want a bounded output and an immediate stop so a divergent experiment remains controlled.

stories.outcome: Every session and its settings and results are stored locally; the engineer can browse and reload sessions and compare two by band, with delta defined as b minus a.
stories.story: As an audio engineer, I want to revisit and compare experiments so I can identify which configuration improved each band.

stories.outcome: The engineer can start runs, browse, reload and compare in the local page, or run, list, show and export through the CLI, without accounts or network access.
stories.story: As an audio engineer, I want a usable local instrument and scriptable CLI so I can work interactively or repeat experiments from commands.

vision.understanding: Quiet Bench helps an audio engineer decide which noise-cancellation ideas deserve hardware investment by running controlled offline simulations, reporting trustworthy band-by-band results and enabling safe comparison of saved experiments.
users: Audio engineer exploring noise-cancellation ideas before buying hardware

align.why: The intended user, key decision, interfaces, safety behavior and constraints are sufficiently specified. The observed Node discrepancy is a verification limitation, not a change to the requested Node 20 constraint; no material product choice remains to ask before the user decides gate A.
